questions.q: For the directed line from P(2,3,5) to Q(-1,2,4), what are its direction cosines?
questions.explanation: The direction ratios from P to Q are Q-P=(-3,-1,-1). Their magnitude is sqrt(9+1+1)=sqrt(11). Dividing each ratio by sqrt(11) gives the stated direction cosines for the directed line P to Q.

questions.q: Find the perpendicular distance of the point with position vector 2i+j-k from the plane r.(i-2j+4k)=9.
questions.explanation: The point is (2,1,-1) and the plane is x-2y+4z-9=0. Substitution in the numerator gives |2-2-4-9|=13. The normal has magnitude sqrt(1+4+16)=sqrt(21), so the distance is 13/sqrt(21).

questions.q: The line through (3,-4,-5) and (2,-3,1) meets the plane through (2,2,1), (3,0,1) and (4,-1,0). What is the intersection point?
questions.explanation: The plane through the three points reduces to 2x+y+z-7=0. A point on the line can be written as (3-lambda,-4+lambda,-5+6lambda). Substitution into the plane gives lambda=2, hence the intersection point is (1,-2,7).

questions.q: What is the image of P(1,6,3) in the line x/1=(y-1)/2=(z-2)/3?
questions.explanation: A general point on the line is L=(lambda,2lambda+1,3lambda+2). Requiring PL to be perpendicular to direction (1,2,3) gives lambda=1, so the foot is L=(1,3,5). Since L is the midpoint of P and its image Q, Q=2L-P=(1,0,7).
